objects.name: TLCTC Project
objects.description: Publisher of the Top Level Cyber Threat Clusters (TLCTC) framework, v2.6. https://www.tlctc.net

objects.name: TLCTC for Attack Flow
objects.description: Adds TLCTC v2.6 cause classification to Attack Flow objects: on attack-action the cause cluster (#1..#10) of the step, its operational sub-cluster, the attack velocity to the next step, responsibility-sphere and intra-system boundaries, Data Risk Events, foreign-code execution and the unresolved state; on attack-flow the path-level metadata and notation; on attack-operator the parallel-group metadata. Attack Flow says what the adversary did; this extension says which generic vulnerability each step exploited.

objects.name: SOLARWINDS-SUNBURST-2020
objects.description: SolarWinds SUNBURST supply chain compromise (December 2020). Attack path: #10 ||[update][@Vendor→@Org]|| →[Δt=instant] #7 + [DRE: C] →[Δt=~14d] #4 →[Δt=~2h] #1 + [DRE: C]. APT29/Cozy Bear attributed (Axiom IV: actor identity does not change cluster classification). Sources: CISA Alert AA20-352A, Microsoft MSRC, FireEye/Mandiant UNC2452 report. v2.6 requalification (2026-09-23): this record had not been lifted to v2.5; checked against the v2.5 and v2.6 changes. Classification unchanged; s1 now states the v2.6 subversion test and falsifier. s3 stays #4 without a #10: the forged SAML tokens were signed with the victim organisation's own federation key, not issued by a subverted third-party identity provider.

objects.name: #10 Supply Chain Attack
objects.description: Trust Acceptance Event: SolarWinds Orion update v2019.4-2020.2.1 containing SUNBURST backdoor accepted and installed by target organization via legitimate update channel. The compromised DLL (SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll) was digitally signed by SolarWinds, passing all trust verification. Subversion and falsifiability (v2.6): the vendor build was subverted before the target accepted the update; remove that subversion - SolarWinds shipping its genuine Orion update - and the step fails, so #10 holds.

objects.name: #7 Malware
objects.description: FEC execution via designed capability: SUNBURST backdoor DLL loaded and executed by the legitimate SolarWinds Orion service (solarwinds.businesslayerhost.exe). The execution used the environment's intended DLL loading mechanism — an intended data→code transition, not an exploit. SUNBURST remained dormant for approximately 12-14 days before activating C2 communication via DNS (avsvmcloud.com). R-EXEC satisfied: FEC execution recorded as #7. [DRE: C] is recorded here: host and domain profiling was sent to the C2 channel, and the SAML token-signing certificate was obtained during this step. Per Axiom X the acquisition of credential material maps to the enabling cluster, which is this #7 step, so the confidentiality event belongs here and not on the #4 step that later presents the forged token.

objects.name: #4 Identity Theft
objects.description: Credential application: attacker forged SAML tokens using stolen signing certificates to impersonate legitimate users and access cloud resources (Azure AD, Office 365). Per Axiom X and R-CRED, the acquisition of the signing key occurred during the #7 step and its confidentiality event is recorded there; the USE of forged credentials to authenticate is always #4 regardless of acquisition method. This step carries no DRE of its own: authenticating discloses nothing, alters nothing and denies nothing. The disclosure it enables is recorded where it occurs, on the #1 step that reads mail through the designed cloud APIs — attaching [DRE: C] here as well would count the same exfiltration twice and would judge the step by what the attacker later obtained rather than by what this step did.

objects.name: #1 Abuse of Functions
objects.description: Abuse of legitimate cloud functions: attacker used valid (forged) credentials to abuse Azure AD APIs, Office 365 mail reading APIs, and federated trust configurations for data exfiltration. No code flaw exploited — the attacker operated within the designed functionality of the cloud platform using stolen identity. Data stayed data; no foreign code was introduced at this stage.
